rubriker.title: 7/7 points, rating performance 2955!
rubriker._rss_content: We have seen a lot of great performances at the Olympiad in Samarkand – many great players have lived up to their high standards. But it is especially pleasing to see chess prodigies you have known and looked after since their early teens deliver the goods. Like this batch, who have been surging. One has scored in absolutely record-breaking style. You'll never guess who.

rubriker.title: Samarkand R8 (open): Germany stun Uzbekistan, join them in the lead
rubriker._rss_content: Germany ended Uzbekistan's perfect run in round eight of the Chess Olympiad, beating the hosts 2½–1½ to join them on 14/16 match points. Brothers Frederik and Rasmus Svane (pictured) collected wins for Germany on the bottom boards for a second day in a row. Eight teams now sit only one point behind, including China, India, the United States and the Netherlands. With three rounds remaining, the standings have tightened considerably ahead of another set of direct clashes among the leading teams. | Photo: Michal Walusza / FIDE

rubriker.title: Bodhana Sivanandan: Chess and other passions
rubriker._rss_content: Bodhana Sivanandan is only eleven years old, but in Samarkand she is already playing in her second Olympiad. And with considerable success: after seven rounds, she has scored six points on top board for the England women’s team, corresponding to an Elo performance of 2504. But when she spoke to Arne Kähler, chess was not the only passion they discussed.

rubriker.title: Germany Usmaxxing at the Olympiad
rubriker._rss_content: Jan Gustafsson, coaching Germany's Olympiad team, had some fun with the scale of his team's achievement after round eight's headline win over tournament leaders Uzbekistan: Germany has now beaten all three of Uzbekistan's entered teams.

rubriker.title: FIDE Education Summit in Samarkand Highlights Chess as a Global Educational Tool
rubriker._rss_content: The FIDE Summit in Samarkand highlighted chess as a powerful educational tool, with global initiatives focused on teacher training, school programs, and long-term partnerships to make chess more accessible to children worldwide.

rubriker.title: Turlov and Buettner Participate in LIVE Q&A Session at the Olympiad
rubriker._rss_content: A live Q&A showed Buettner and Turlov offering ambitious, business-driven visions for FIDE, but both left important questions about transparency, accountability, and the risks of concentrating too much influence in a wealthy president unresolved.

rubriker.title: Rosenstein's El País Interview
rubriker._rss_content: El País published an interview with Wadim Rosenstein on September 24, conducted in Samarkand by Leontxo García, two days ahead of the FIDE presidential vote.

rubriker.title: The Svane Brothers End Uzbekistan's Perfect Run
rubriker._rss_content: Round eight delivered the result the Open section had been building toward since Uzbekistan pulled clear of the field two rounds ago: a loss, its first of the tournament, and a home-soil defeat at that.
